phone.description: a phone number, as a component of what it reaches — on a person, their mobile, beside the `email{address}` they wear

own_number.description: a number held by a person's own account at a phone provider, as it was listed when they connected it: what it is called there, whether it texts, and where its texts went before its host pointed them at itself. Its eid is derived from its connection and number

connection.description: the connection to the account that holds it

sms.description: whether it sends and receives texts

label.description: what the account calls it, as the person named it there

callback.description: the URL its texts were sent to before its host pointed them at itself; absent when none was. They go back there when the number stops taking texts in

sms_consent.description: a person agreed to be texted at their `phone{number}`, in these words; removed when they stop texts; in an app, read only by its owners and editors, whatever the app's access

person.description: who agreed; the eid is derived from it, so a person has one consent

consent.description: the words they agreed to, exactly as they were shown

source.description: the conversation entry or authenticated form confirmation that gave this consent

space.description: the space whose Operator texts them: the one they agreed on, and where a text from them goes

text.description: one text message, sent or received; its words are `doc{body}`. One with @yaks/mail's `deliver{to}` asks to be sent to the `phone{number}` of `deliver.to`, and its outcome is `delivered` or `bounced`; in an app, read only by its owners and editors, whatever the app's access

from.description: the number it came from, in E.164 form; on one sent, the number it left from, written once it leaves (absent before, when it goes from the sender's own)

to.description: the number it went to, or the RCS agent's id for an RCS text that arrived; written on one sent once it leaves

message_id.description: the provider's id for it: read from one that arrived, or returned by the sender for one that left

rcs.description: whether it came, or goes, as RCS rather than SMS

via.description: The transport that carried the message, scoping its opaque message_id.

text_post.description: Hand an outbound text to the sender and record its outcome. A send the sender knows never left is tried again.

sender.description: The phone provider selected for this entity; its sending number is phone{number}. Without one the host selection applies. Credentials belong to the host.

via.description: The phone provider, such as telnyx, voipms or pinnacle.

text_send.title: Text a person
text_send.description: Text a person who agreed to be texted, from this graph's own number, through the sender its config names. `to` is the id or name of a person here who wears a `phone{number}` and an `sms_consent`, or that number; anyone else is refused. Their reply arrives as a `text` from their number and is told to the session that texted them. The text goes asynchronously and `delivered` or `bounced` is written onto it; read it again for its outcome. A sent text cannot be recalled.

to.description: the person's id or name, or their number
